newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - ScotPower yr profits pump higher.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - ScotPower yr profits pump higher.

text.p: British energy and water group Scottish Power Plc is expected to pump annual profits substantially higher when it reports on May 15, helped by last year's purchase of Southern Water, but analysts said attention will focus on its ability to show its multi-utility strategy is working.
"That's the real challenge over the next two to three years, cross-selling of services after all its acquisitions," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

Scottish Power is expected to turn in pretax profits between 538.3 and 582 million stg compared with 404.8 million stg previously and has already said it aims to pay a dividend of 18.5 pence, up from 15.5 pence a year ago.
Analysts said there could be restructuring charges of around 30-35 million stg.
The leap in profits is in large part attributable to the contribution of Southern Water, the water and sewerage company that Scottish Power snapped up for 1.68 billion stg last summer, analysts said.
Scottish Power bought regional electricity company (Rec) Manweb in 1995, becoming the first and only British electricity generator to be allowed to buy a Rec.
The company also has gas and telecommunications interests.

Scottish Power said in December that it had plans to improve pretax profits at Southern Water by 52 million stg a year, with 2,050 job losses as well, as aiming to release some 100 million stg from the water utility.
"We will be looking for some reassurance on the whole multi-utility strategy," the analyst said.
Britain boasts two other multi-utilities, Hyder, which was formed when Welsh Water bought South Wales Electricity, and United Utilities, which groups North West Water and Norweb.
Scottish Power has already started selling gas to Southern Water customers in trials ahead of liberalisation of the gas and electricity markets, scheduled for 1998.
"We will be looking for progress on cost cutting, disposals, for Scottish Power to show the fruits of its aggressive acquisition strategy," the analyst said.
The company could also provide indications on plans at its telecommunications business, where it hopes to take a slice of the Scottish market from British Telecommunications (BT).
"We'll be looking to see breakeven or even a light profit in telecommunications this year," the analyst said.

There is some debate over whether Scottish Power will be subjected to a one-off "windfall" tax planned by the new Labour government and at what level this might be, but analysts said the company was unlikely to make any comment at this stage. -- Jo Winterbottom, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
